edition.name: 'Self-Help; with Illustrations of Conduct and Perseverance', by Samuel Smiles, LL.D., John Murray edition of 1897, Project Gutenberg eBook #935, released 28 December 2014 (first posted 10 June 1997), transcribed by David Price
edition.status: The file's own header reads "Transcribed from the 1897 John Murray edition by David Price", so the printing is named: John Murray, 1897. The text is a later revised printing of the 1859 book, not the first edition: footnotes in it refer to "this revised edition" and to events as late as 1866. The file holds a preface dated September 1859, the contents, thirteen chapters and a block of footnotes. No introduction or notes by another hand appear in the file. The edition year is taken from the file header only and is not yet checked against a second source [to confirm]. The workbook draws on six chapters (I, IV, VIII, X, XI and XIII), see the chapter selection below.

modernisation.rulesApplied: Reversible rules only (MODERNISATION_RULES in packages/validate/src/classics.ts). Spelling and typography, nothing that changes a word's meaning.
modernisation.revertChecked: Reverting the committed log on the modernised text returns the cut source byte for byte (833,526 bytes, sha1 64876da9641f36b5df62ef3365ac89affc1fc6b7).
modernisation.logFormat: The same entries the script writes, one entry per line to keep the file small.
modernisation.knownIssue: The em-dash rule writes a comma and a space. Where the printed text had a comma before the dash, the result is a doubled comma. There are 140 in the whole text. No quotation in the workbook includes one, and each quotation was cut to avoid them. A tooling fix (consume the preceding comma) is a separate commit.
modernisation.outsideTheRules: Smiles's 1897 spellings (labour, honour, civilisation) are already British. Italic markers in the transcription (underscores) are left out of every quotation, and no quotation spans one. The workbook's own prose is en-GB.
modernisation.editorial: No [Editorial] changes were made. Quotations are exact, checked by chapter against the modernised copy.

selection.why: The book runs to about 139,700 words in the cut text. The catalogue length is six weeks, so six chapters are selected, one a week. The other seven are not summarised.
selection.chapterWordsRead: About 62,700 of about 135,400 words of chapter text (footnotes excluded).

notUsed.II: Leaders of Industry, inventors and producers

selection.reasons: Chapters II, III, V, VI and VII are long runs of lives of inventors, potters, scientists, artists and peers, and add examples rather than new ideas. Chapters IX and XII overlap with the chapters kept (time and order sit in Chapter IV, example and influence in Chapters I and XIII) and can be added if the programme is lengthened.
selection.differsFromCatalogue: The catalogue outline (weeks 3 and 4: small things and use of time; weeks 5 and 6: money, character and the people who helped you) predates the selection. The workbook follows the usual spine instead: self-help, application and perseverance, energy and courage, money, self-culture, character. Use of time is covered inside Chapter IV (Buffon, Scott, Drew) and Chapter XI (spare minutes). The people who helped you are covered in Chapter I (de Tocqueville). The catalogue outline in docs/planning is not edited here.
selection.cutsWithinChapters: Recorded in the workbook's internal.cut_log: war, empire and race passages in Chapter VIII; health and exercise passages in Chapter XI; drink, class and religious passages in Chapter X; the imperial heroes at the end of Chapter XIII.
selection.claimsCare: No income, wellbeing, health or treatment claim appears. Money passages that promise prosperity (for example Lord Erskine's "road to prosperity and wealth" in Chapter XIII) are not quoted. The money unit says in its introduction that it gives no financial advice and makes no promise about money, and its exercises ask for no amounts.
